title: AWQ & FP8 compatibility validation and pinned-rollout workflow for quant profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Create an end-to-end onboarding and validation flow for non-standard quant formats (AWQ, FP8) in addition to existing GPTQ/INT8 paths, and wire that flow into the pinned-model rollout system so that performance regressions are detected before any customer-facing pin. Deliverables: 1) validation matrix (accuracy/latency/memory) per format per hardware profile, 2) automated CI jobs that publish a validated quant profile artifact to the catalog, 3) a pinned-rollout checklist + canary policy for rolling a quantized model into Dedicated/Private, 4) alerting rules and dashboards that surface perf regressions tied to profile publishes. Scope: - Support AWQ and FP8 conversion pipelines in the model-onboarding repo - Extend perf-benchmark harness to compare baseline fp16 vs quant variant using standard eval sets and synthetic latency traces - Update model-catalog metadata to include quant_format, quant_tool_version, measured_latency_p50/p95, perf_ci_sha - Add a pre-publish gating job that rejects a profile if latency increase > 20% or eval-score drop > configurable threshold - Integrate result link into Console's rollout UI to allow engineers/PMs to approve or block pinning. Out of scope: retraining or model architecture changes.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Kickoff: scoped with Model Onboarding and Runtime teams. Agreed to prioritize AWQ and FP8 due to customer requests from enterprise sales.
2026-03-03 - Design review: Lena (Runtime) suggested adding an ephemeral KV cache stress test for AWQ because AWQ memory layout amplifies cache thrash. Action: add KV stress job to perf harness.

2026-03-06 - Engineering spike complete: successful AWQ conversion for small GPT-like model locally; p50 latency regressed ~8% on A100, p95 ~18% on T4. Added baseline scripts to repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboarding/pull/321
2026-03-08 - PM feedback: require a threshold matrix per customer tier and a manual approval step for P0 customers. Added to checklist.

2026-03-10 - CI work: prototype GitHub Actions job that runs eval + latency runner and uploads artifacts to the internal S3 catalog. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboarding/pull/333 (WIP)

2026-03-12 - Observability alignment: connected with Console team to define rollout UI hooks. Draft dashboard for quant-profile publishes posted: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Quant+Profile+Publishes

2026-03-13 - Blocker discovered: FP8 conversion tool emits non-deterministic attention kernels on CUDA 12.2 which causes flaky p95 numbers. Created follow-up task with Runtime for kernel deterministic mode. Assigned to ENG-11602.

2026-03-14 - Current: CI prototype uploads metrics but gating rules not enforced. Next: add automated reject step and wire to catalog publish API, add canary rollout integration, and run full validation matrix across target hardware.
acceptance_criteria: Automated CI validates AWQ and FP8 quant profiles and produces a signed artifact in model-catalog with metadata fields (quant_format, quant_tool_version, measured_latency_p50, measured_latency_p95, eval_score).
Gating policy enforced: publish blocked if p50 increases >20% or eval_score drops beyond profile-specific threshold. Thresholds configurable per project.
Pinned rollout flow requires explicit approval for P0 customers and supports automatic canary traffic at 1%, 10%, 100% with automated rollback on perf alerts.
Dashboards and alerts exist that link a profile publish to observed downstream latency/regression metrics within the first 24h of rollout.
qa_plan: Run the onboarding CI against 3 representative models (small, medium, large) on three hardware profiles (A100, T4, AMD MI300) using both AWQ and FP8 conversions. Validate deterministic outputs for eval sets and capture latency percentiles under synthetic load. Execute canary rollout in staging and simulate perf degradation to verify rollback triggers.
risks: Non-deterministic FP8 kernels on some CUDA/toolchain combinations causing noisy p95 measurements.
AWQ memory layout could increase memory pressure and cause OOMs on constrained Dedicated instances if batch sizes not autotuned.
Overly strict gating thresholds may block safe optimizations; too loose thresholds may let regressions through. Need calibration and historical baselines.
next_steps: Finish kernel determinism investigation (ENG-11602) and add deterministic mode to FP8 toolchain by 2026-03-18.
Complete CI gating implementation and add automated reject/publish step in model-catalog by 2026-03-21.
Run full validation matrix across target hardware and publish results to Confluence; iterate thresholds with PM by 2026-03-24.
Wire published profile metadata into Console rollout UI and add approval button for P0 customers by 2026-03-28.
